chunks.text: 54-year-old female, Homemaker, resident of Tanglin, Singapore.
Fractured wrist (20 years ago, full recovery)
Irritable bowel syndrome (no active symptoms for 5 years)
General Anesthesia with Laryngeal Mask Airway (LMA)

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning! I'm going to be your anesthesiologist for your upcoming cholecystectomy. Can you please start by telling me a bit about your medical history and why you're having this surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Morning, doc. Yeah, I've been having a lot of tummy pains, especially after eating. The scans showed gallstones, so the doctor said it's best to take out the gallbladder. Hope that fixes the problem, lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for sharing that. Now, let's go over your medications. I see you're on Atorvastatin, Metformin, Lisinopril, and Aspirin. Can you confirm if you're still taking all of these, and if not, what changes have been made?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Ah, the Aspirin... I stopped that about six months ago because it was giving me bad stomach issues, like acid or something. My heart doctor then put me on Clopidogrel 75 mg daily instead for protection.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for clarifying that. It's important we have the most current medication list. Just to confirm, are you still taking Atorvastatin 20 mg daily, Metformin 500 mg twice daily, and Lisinopril 10 mg daily without any issues?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, doc, all those are still the same. No problems with them, touch wood.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Now, about allergies, we have you down as allergic to Penicillin with a rash. Has there been any other allergic reactions to foods, medications, or latex that we should know about?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, just the Penicillin. That's the only one.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia? If so, how did you tolerate them?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Once, for my appendix, about ten years back. I was under general, and I woke up with a sore throat, but that was about it. No other issues, I think.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: A sore throat can be a common side effect. We'll note that. Now, regarding your diabetes, how have you been managing it? Are your blood sugars under good control with Metformin?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yeah, I check regularly. Sometimes it fluctuates, but generally, it's okay. My HbA1c was 7.2% at the last check, I think.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to hear. Finally, for this surgery, we're planning for general anesthesia with a Laryngeal Mask Airway (LMA). Have you had any issues with breathing or airway problems in the past that we should be aware of?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doc, I don't think so. Breathing's always been fine for me.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: And just to confirm, when's the last time you had anything to eat or drink? We need to ensure you're NPO (nil per os) status is appropriate for surgery.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I had dinner around 8 pm last night and just water this morning, but nothing after midnight, as instructed.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect, thank you. I think that covers everything. Do you have any questions for me about the anesthesia or the procedure?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doc, I think you've covered it all. Just ready to get this done.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] tube in, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] fentanyl fifty micrograms

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] rocuronium thirty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] LMA sixteen in place

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] lactated ringers one liter bolus

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:30] mean arterial pressure dropped to fifty five, atenolol ten milligrams IV

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:40] surgery started

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [09:00] desflurane at six percent

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [09:20] blood pressure stable after fluid bolus, heart rate seventy

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Still a bit groggy, but okay. My tummy is sore, though.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: I understand. Can you rate your pain for me, from 1 to 10?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Hmm, maybe a 4 or 5. It's manageable, but I can feel it.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. Have you been feeling nauseous or sick to your stomach at all?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: A little bit when I first woke up, but it's better now. Not too bad.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. How's your breathing? Any discomfort or feeling like you can't catch your breath?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I'm breathing fine. My throat is a bit sore, but that's all.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That can happen with the LMA. Do you remember anything from the surgery itself?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, nothing. I was out cold. Just woke up here.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's expected. Since you have hypertension and diabetes, we'll keep a close eye on your vitals and blood sugar levels. Any concerns from your side?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think I'm okay. Just want to go home and rest.

54-year-old female undergoing elective cholecystectomy for symptomatic gallstones.
Patient has controlled Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (HbA1c 7.2%), hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. Current medications include Metformin, Lisinopril, Atorvastatin, and Clopidogrel.
Patient has a penicillin allergy (rash) and no other known allergies.
Patient is NPO since midnight, with last meal at 8 pm and only water thereafter.

Intraoperative course included general anesthesia with LMA, induction with Propofol and Fentanyl, muscle relaxation with Rocuronium, and fluid resuscitation with 1 liter Lactated Ringer's. Transient hypotension (MAP 55 mmHg) occurred but stabilized with fluid bolus.
Anticipated postoperative concerns include PONV, airway complications due to LMA, glycemic control, postoperative pain, and potential for antibiotic adjustment due to penicillin allergy.

Monitor for signs of PONV, ensure airway patency post-extubation, maintain glycemic control, manage postoperative pain appropriately, and be vigilant for signs of hypotension or hemodynamic instability.
Patient reports being 'a bit groggy' post-operatively.
Patient experiences abdominal soreness at the surgical site, rating pain as 4 or 5 out of 10.
Patient reports initial nausea upon waking, which has since improved.
Patient denies any breathing discomfort or difficulty catching breath.
Patient reports a sore throat, attributed to the Laryngeal Mask Airway (LMA).
Patient has no recall of the surgery itself, as expected under general anesthesia.
Patient's blood pressure was stable post-fluid bolus during surgery, with a heart rate of 70.
Patient's diabetes and hypertension will be closely monitored post-operatively.
